title: Staged tool-pipeline execution, deterministic injection order, and idempotent replay for parallel calls
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a staged execution mode for multi-tool pipelines and an idempotent replay mechanism for safe retries. Improves deterministic injection ordering for tool results. Opt-in runtime flag; SDK adapters updated.
description:
Motivation: multi-tool patterns (parallel calls, fan-in injection) increased nondeterminism in how tool outputs were injected into the model prompt and streaming responses. This caused intermittent flakiness in structured outputs and made retries unsafe for side-effectful tools. This PR introduces a staged execution model and idempotent replay primitives to make multi-tool executions deterministic, safe to retry, and compatible with existing OpenAI-style function calling semantics.

What this changes (summary):
- Introduce a runtime 'staged' pipeline for tool calls: tools are scheduled into deterministic stages (prepare -> call -> collect -> inject) to guarantee a stable injection order across parallel executions.
- Add a gating/semaphore layer that limits in-flight tool calls per-request and enforces backpressure to protect downstream serving resources.
- Implement an idempotent replay token and deterministic result hash so retries can be replayed without duplicate side effects (requires tool adapter support).
- Update the OpenAI compatibility layer so function-call responses preserve staged injection metadata; no caller-facing API breaking changes — current behavior preserved unless staged mode is enabled.
- Add SDK shims (python/ts) that expose an opt-in 'staged' flag when calling tools or using run_tool_chain; adapters updated to support idempotent hooks.
- Improved telemetry: new metrics for stage latencies, semaphore contention, and replay counts.

Design notes:
- Determinism is achieved by assigning stable sort keys to tool requests (source order + tie-breaker) before parallel dispatch. We batch by stage so KV/cache insertion and prompt injection happen in a single deterministic pass.
- Replay token is generated from request id + stage metadata. Tool adapters must implement a replay check to short-circuit side effects; a fallback safe-execute path is provided for older adapters.
- Backpressure gating uses a leaky-bucket semaphore per-tenant that integrates with existing autoscaling hooks to avoid queuing storms during traffic spikes.

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests for stage ordering, simulated parallel tool calls, and replay idempotency.
- End-to-end tests included in perf-canary harness to validate latency tail at 95/99 pctl under staged mode.
- Manual regression checks against OpenAI compatibility matrix to ensure function-calling payloads remain unchanged when staged mode is off.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind ENABLE_STAGED_TOOL_PIPELINE (runtime config).
- Default: off. Rollout plan: 1) internal dogfood 0->10% for 48h, 2) 10->50% for 72h if metrics stable, 3) 100% after 7 days with opt-in telemetry retained for 30d.

Backward compatibility: staged mode is opt-in; existing customers see no change unless they enable the flag. SDKs provide transparent shims so older clients will continue to work.

Related: ENG-1942, SUP-712.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler and replay primitives
- [x] E2E tests in perf-canary
- [x] SDK adapters updated (python/ts)

review_comments: Omar Ruiz: Overall this looks good. Two asks: add a diagram in the RFC for stage transitions and ensure semaphore defaults are conservative. Also add a brief cookbook section for adapter authors.
Maya Chen: Thanks Omar — added diagram to RFC and included adapter cookbook in docs. Default semaphore capacities set to conservative values and moved to config with tenant override.
Elliot Park: The replay_token path looks sensible but we need a migration plan for adapters that don't honor idempotency. Can we have a 'safe-execute' fallback with explicit audit logs?

Maya Chen: Added safe-execute fallback and an audit log entry emitted when fallback is used. Documented in adapters.md. Also added an integration test that simulates a legacy adapter to verify no double side-effects.
Lucia Fernandez: CI flaky on one e2e — the perf-canary job timed out once. Reran CI and verified metrics. Approving once CI green.
Lucia Fernandez: Approve — LGTM (post-approval tweak: added more assert messaging in unit tests)
notes_on_rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag ENABLE_STAGED_TOOL_PIPELINE; default off for 2 weeks, gradual rollout to 100% with telemetry. Tenant override available for large customers.
compatibility_notes: OpenAI-compatible function-calling surface preserved when staged mode is off. When staged mode is on, function-call responses include an extra internal 'staged_metadata' field consumed by SDK adapters; SDKs hide this from end-users. No breaking API changes for callers.
changelog_entry: Staged tool pipeline (opt-in): deterministic injection order, idempotent replay for safe retries, semaphore-based backpressure
